question: What is the role of conscience in Catholic moral teaching?

choices.A: Conscience is the proximate norm of morality — the practical judgment of reason about the moral quality of a particular act — but it must be formed by truth and right reason
choices.B: Conscience is irrelevant; only the Church's formal teaching determines moral obligation
choices.C: Conscience is the ultimate norm with no need of formation or correction
choices.D: Conscience applies only to non-Catholics; Catholics are bound purely by Church law

teaching.title: Conscience in Catholic Moral Theology
teaching.body: The Catechism (CCC 1776) calls conscience 'a judgment of reason whereby the human person recognizes the moral quality of a concrete act.' Vatican II's Gaudium et Spes (16) says 'in the depths of his conscience, man detects a law which he does not impose upon himself, but which holds him to obedience.' However, a conscience must be correctly formed — an erroneous conscience that is culpably uninformed is still morally responsible. The tension: the person must always follow their conscience, but they have a duty to form it correctly. 'Conscience is the most secret core and sanctuary of a person' (GS 16).
